questions.q: The sum of all possible values of $\theta \in[-\pi, 2 \pi]$, for which $\frac{1+i \cos \theta}{1-2 i \cos \theta}$ is purely imaginary, is equal
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & Z=\frac{1+i \cos \theta}{1-2 i \cos \theta} \\ & Z=-\bar{Z} \Rightarrow \frac{1+i \cos \theta}{1-2 i \cos \theta}=-\left(\frac{\overline{1+i \cos \theta}}{1-2 i \cos \theta}\right) \\ & (1+i \cos \theta)(\overline{1-2 i \cos \theta})=-(1-2 i \cos \theta)(\overline{1+i \cos \theta}) \\ & (1+i \cos \theta)(1+2 i \cos \theta)=-(1-2 i \cos \theta)(1-i \cos \theta) \\ & 1+3 i \cos \theta-2 \cos ^2 \theta=-\left(1-3 i \cos \theta-2 \cos ^2 \theta\right) \\ & 2-4 \cos ^2 \theta=0 \\ & \Rightarrow \cos ^2 \theta=\frac{1}{2} \Rightarrow \theta=-\frac{\pi}{4},-\frac{3 \pi}{4}, \frac{\pi}{4}, \frac{3 \pi}{4}, \frac{5 \pi}{4}, \frac{7 \pi}{4} \\ & \text { sum }=3 \pi\end{aligned}$

For $\mathrm{a}, \mathrm{b} \gt 0$, let $f(x)=\left\{\begin{array}{cc}\frac{\tan ((\mathrm{a}+1) x)+\mathrm{b} \tan x}{x}, & x \lt  0 \\ 3, & x=0 \\ \frac{\sqrt{\mathrm{a} x+\mathrm{b}^2 x^2}-\sqrt{\mathrm{a} x}}{\mathrm{~b} \sqrt{\mathrm{a}} x \sqrt{x}}, & x \gt 0\end{array}\right.$
be a continous function at $x=0$. Then $\frac{\mathrm{b}}{\mathrm{a}}$ is equal to :
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \lim _{x \rightarrow 0} f(x)=f(0)=3 \\ & \lim _{x \rightarrow 0^{+}} \frac{\sqrt{a x+b^2 x^2}-\sqrt{a x}}{b \sqrt{a} x \sqrt{x}}=3 \\ & \lim _{x \rightarrow 0^{+}} \frac{a x+b^2 x^2-a x}{b \sqrt{a} x^{3 / 2}\left(\sqrt{a x+b^2 x^2}+\sqrt{a x}\right)} \\ & \lim _{x \rightarrow 0^{+}} \frac{b^2}{b \sqrt{a}\left(\sqrt{a+b^2 x}+\sqrt{a}\right)} \\ & \frac{b}{\sqrt{a} \cdot 2 \sqrt{a}} \Rightarrow \frac{b}{2 a}=3 \Rightarrow \frac{b}{a}=6\end{aligned}$

questions.q: Let $y=y(x)$ be the solution curve of the differential equation $\sec y \frac{\mathrm{d} y}{\mathrm{~d} x}+2 x \sin y=x^3 \cos y, y(1)=0$. Then $y(\sqrt{3})$ is equal to :
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \sec ^2 y \frac{d y}{d x}+2 x \sin y \text { secy }=x^3 \cos y \text { secy } \\ & \sec ^2 y \frac{d y}{d x}+2 x \tan y=x^3 \\ & \operatorname{tany}=t \Rightarrow \sec ^2 y \frac{d y}{d x}=\frac{d t}{d x} \\ & \frac{d t}{d x}+2 x t=x^3, \text { If }=e^{\int 2 x d x}=e^{x^2} \\ & t x^{x^2}=\int x^3 \cdot e^{x^2} d x+c \\ & x^2=Z \Rightarrow t \cdot e^Z=\frac{1}{2} \int e^Z \cdot Z d Z=\frac{1}{2}\left[e^Z \cdot Z-e^Z\right]+c \\ & 2 \tan y=\left(x^2-1\right)+2 e^{-x^2} \\ & y(1)=0 \Rightarrow c=0 \Rightarrow y(\sqrt{3})=\frac{\pi}{4}\end{aligned}$

questions.q: Let $\alpha|x|=|y| \mathrm{e}^{x y-\beta}, \alpha, \beta \in \mathbf{N}$ be the solution of the differential equation $x \mathrm{~d} y-y \mathrm{~d} x+x y(x \mathrm{~d} y+y \mathrm{~d} x)=0$, $y(1)=2$. Then $\alpha+\beta$ is equal to ________
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned}
& a|x|=|y| e^{y x-\beta}, a, b \in N \\
& x d y-y d x+x y(x d y+y d x)=0 \\
& \frac{d y}{y}-\frac{d x}{x}+(x d y+y d x)=0 \\
& \ell n|y|-\ell n|x|+x y=c \\
& y(1)=2 \\
& \ell n|2|-0+2=c \\
& c=2+\ell n 2 \\
& \ell n|y|-\ell n|x|+x y=2+\ell n 2 \\
& \ell n|x|=\ell n\left|\frac{y}{2}\right|-2+x y \\
& |x|=\left|\frac{y}{2}\right| e^{x y-2} \\
& 2|x|=|y| e^{x y-2} \\
& \alpha=2 \quad \beta=2 \quad \alpha+\beta=4
\end{aligned}$

questions.q: If $\int \frac{1}{\sqrt[5]{(x-1)^4(x+3)^6}} \mathrm{~d} x=\mathrm{A}\left(\frac{\alpha x-1}{\beta x+3}\right)^B+\mathrm{C}$, where $\mathrm{C}$ is the constant of integration, then the value of $\alpha+\beta+20 \mathrm{AB}$ is__________
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \int \frac{1}{\sqrt[5]{(x-1)^4(x+3)^6}} d x=A\left(\frac{\alpha x-1}{\beta x+3}\right)^B+C \\ & I=\int \frac{1}{(x-1)^{4 / 5}(x+3)^{6 / 5}} d x \\ & I=\int \frac{1}{\left(\frac{x-1}{x+3}\right)^{4 / 5}(x+3)^2} d x \\ & \left(\frac{x-1}{x+3}\right)=t \Rightarrow \frac{4}{(x+3)^2} d x=d t \quad t^{-4 / 5+1} \\ & I=\frac{1}{4} \int \frac{1}{t^{4 / 5}} d t=\frac{1}{4} \frac{t^{1 / 5}}{1 / 5}+c \\ & I=\frac{5}{4}\left(\frac{x-1}{x+3}\right)^{1 / 5}+C \\ & A=\frac{5}{4} \quad \alpha=\beta=1 \quad B=\frac{1}{5} \\ & \alpha+\beta+20 A B=2+20 \times \frac{5}{4} \times \frac{1}{5}=7\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $\alpha=\lim _{x \rightarrow 0^{+}}\left(\frac{\mathrm{e}^{\sqrt{\tan x}}-\mathrm{e}^{\sqrt{x}}}{\sqrt{\tan x}-\sqrt{x}}\right)$ and $\beta=\lim _{x \rightarrow 0}(1+\sin x)^{\frac{1}{2} \cot x}$ are the roots of the quadratic equation $a x^2+b x-\sqrt{\mathrm{e}}=0$, then $12 \log _{\mathrm{e}}(\mathrm{a}+\mathrm{b})$ is equal to__________
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \alpha=\lim _{x \rightarrow 0^{+}} e^{\sqrt{x}} \frac{\left(e^{\sqrt{\tan x}-\sqrt{x}}-1\right)}{\sqrt{\tan x}-\sqrt{x}} \\ & =1 \\ & \beta=\lim _{x \rightarrow 0}(1+\sin x)^{\frac{1}{2} \cot x} \\ & =e^{1 / 2} \\ & x^2-(1+\sqrt{e})+\sqrt{e}=0 \\ & a x^2+b x-\sqrt{e}=0 \\ & \text { On comparing } \\ & a=-1, b=\sqrt{e}+1 \\ & 12 \ln (a+b)=12 \times \frac{1}{2}=6\end{aligned}$

questions.q: Let $A=\{2,3,6,8,9,11\}$ and $B=\{1,4,5,10,15\}$. Let $R$ be a relation on $A \times B$ defined by $(a, b) R(c, d)$ if and only if $3 a d-7 b c$ is an even integer. Then the relation $R$ is
options: reflexive and symmetric but not transitive.
questions.solution:
$\begin{array}{lc}\mathrm{A}=\{2,3,6,8,9,11\} & (\mathrm{a}, \mathrm{b}) \mathrm{R}(\mathrm{c}, \mathrm{d}) \\ \mathrm{B}=\{1,4,5,10,15\} & 3 \mathrm{ad}-7 \mathrm{bc}\end{array}$
Reflexive : $(\mathrm{a}, \mathrm{b}) \mathrm{R}(\mathrm{a}, \mathrm{b})\Rightarrow 3 \mathrm{ab}-7 \mathrm{ba}=-4 \mathrm{ab}$ always even so it is reflexive.
Symmetric : If $3 \mathrm{ad}-7 \mathrm{bc}=$ Even
Case-I : odd odd
Case-II : even even
(c, d) $\mathrm{R}(\mathrm{a}, \mathrm{b}) \Rightarrow 3 \mathrm{bc}-3 \mathrm{ab}$
Case-I : odd odd
Case-II : even even
so symmetric relation
Transitive :
Set $(3,4) R(6,4)$ Satisfy relation
Set $(6,4) R(3,1)$ Satisfy relation
but $(3,4) \mathrm{R}(3,1)$ does not satisfy relation so not transitive.

questions.q: Let $\mathrm{a}, \mathrm{b}, \mathrm{c} \in \mathrm{N}$ and $\mathrm{a} \lt  \mathrm{b} \lt  \mathrm{c}$. Let the mean, the mean deviation about the mean and the variance of the 5 observations $9,25, \mathrm{a}, \mathrm{b}, \mathrm{c}$ be 18,4 and $\frac{136}{5}$, respectively. Then $2 \mathrm{a}+\mathrm{b}-\mathrm{c}$ is equal to__________
questions.solution:
$a, b, c \in N \quad a \lt  b \lt  c\overline{\mathrm{x}}=$ mean $=\frac{9+25+\mathrm{a}+\mathrm{b}+\mathrm{c}}{5}=18a+b+c=56$
Mean deviation $=\frac{\Sigma\left|\mathrm{x}_{\mathrm{i}}-\overline{\mathrm{x}}\right|}{\mathrm{n}}=4\begin{aligned} & =9+7+|18-\mathrm{a}|+|18-\mathrm{b}|+|18-\mathrm{c}|=20 \\ & =|18-\mathrm{a}|+|18-\mathrm{b}|+|18-\mathrm{c}|=4\end{aligned}$
Variance $=\frac{\Sigma\left|\mathrm{x}_{\mathrm{i}}-\overline{\mathrm{x}}\right|^2}{\mathrm{n}}=\frac{136}{5}\begin{aligned} & =81+49+|18-a|^2+|18-b|^2+|18-c|^2=136 \\ & =(18-a)^2+(18-b)^2+(18-c)^2=6\end{aligned}$
Possible values $(18-\mathrm{a})^2=1, \quad(18-\mathrm{b})^2=1 \quad(18-\mathrm{c})^2=4\mathrm{a} \lt  \mathrm{b} \lt  \mathrm{c}$
so $\quad \begin{array}{ccc}18-a=1 & 18-b=-1 & 18-c=-2 \\ \mathrm{a}=17 & \mathrm{~b}=19 & \mathrm{c}=20\end{array}
$a+b+c=562 \mathrm{a}+\mathrm{b}-\mathrm{c} 34=19-20=33

questions.solution:
Image of point $(-4,5)\frac{x-x_1}{a}=\frac{y-y_1}{b}=-2\left(\frac{a x_1+b y_1+c}{a^2+b^2}\right)$
Line: $x+2 y-2=0\frac{x+4}{1}=\frac{y-5}{2}=-2\left(\frac{-4+10-2}{1^2+2^2}\right)=\frac{-8}{5}x=-4-\frac{8}{5}=-\frac{28}{5}y=-\frac{16}{5}+5=\frac{9}{5}$
Point lies on circle $(x+4)^2+(y-3)^2=r^2\begin{aligned} & \frac{64}{25}+\left(\frac{9}{5}-3\right)^2=r^2 \\ & \frac{100}{25}=r^2, r=2\end{aligned}$

questions.solution: Case-1 : No friction $\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{a}=\mathrm{g} \sin \theta \\ & \ell=\frac{1}{2}(\mathrm{~g} \sin \theta) \mathrm{t}_1^2 \\ & \mathrm{t}_1=\sqrt{\frac{2 \ell}{\mathrm{g} \sin \theta}} \end{aligned}$ Case-2 : With friction $\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{a}=\mathrm{g} \sin \theta-\mu \mathrm{g} \cos \theta \\ & \ell=\frac{1}{2}(\mathrm{~g} \sin \theta-\mu \mathrm{g} \cos \theta) \mathrm{t}_2^2 \\ & \sqrt{\frac{2 \ell}{\mathrm{g} \sin \theta-\mu g \cos \theta}}=\mathrm{n} \sqrt{\frac{2 \ell}{\mathrm{g} \sin \theta}} \\ & \mu=1-\frac{1}{\mathrm{n}^2} \end{aligned}$
